objectives.title: Find details in a short text

lessons.explanation: Use estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están. Estar locates people and objects and describes states. Write the accents; esta without an accent is not the verb está.
commonMistakes: Estoy has no written accent; está and están do. Do not apply the regular -ar yo ending to estar.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

lessons.explanation: Use encima de, debajo de, delante de, detrás de and al lado de to locate things. De + el contracts to del, but de la stays separate. Location depends on the stated viewpoint.
examples: El libro está debajo de la mesa.
La silla está al lado del escritorio.
commonMistakes: Do not omit de in debajo de la mesa. De el becomes del.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

lessons.explanation: Usually add -s after a vowel and -es after a consonant. Change final z to c before -es: lápiz → lápices. Articles become los/las or unos/unas. Accents may change as syllables change.
commonMistakes: Do not use el with a plural noun. Lápiz changes spelling and keeps its stressed syllable in lápices.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

lessons.explanation: Read the question first. Find the sentence that gives that detail, and check who, when or where it describes.
examples: ¿Cuándo? Look for the time or day.
commonMistakes: A familiar word alone may not answer the question. Check the whole message.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra strategy lesson; author review, not an independent educator audit.

lessons.explanation: Read the question, then listen for its detail. Replay as needed. Reading the transcript makes it supported practice.
examples: Listen for names, numbers and places.
Replay a short phrase before opening the transcript.
commonMistakes: A familiar word alone may not answer the question. Check the whole message.

stimuli.SpanishText: Mi clase es pequeña. La puerta está al lado de la ventana. El escritorio de la profesora está delante de las mesas. Los libros están encima del escritorio. Mi mochila está debajo de mi silla. Hay dos carteles detrás de la profesora. Nosotros estamos en clase, pero Luis está en la biblioteca. Sus lápices están en una mochila roja cerca de la puerta.
stimuli.provenance: Original fictional passage, authored for Palabra. Not a textbook reading.

stimuli.SpanishText: Los libros están debajo de la mesa.
